predecessors.name: Zand dynasty
predecessors.text: the northern lands the Zand had lost by 1788: Mazandaran, Gilan, Tehran, Qazvin, Hamadan and half of Isfahan, the core Agha Mohammad Khan held when enthroned in 1789

successors.name: Pahlavi dynasty
successors.text: the whole of Iran: the Majles deposed Ahmad Shah on 31 October 1925 and a constituent assembly proclaimed Reza Khan shah on 12 December 1925

ledger.x: 1789: Agha Mohammad Khan founds the Qajar state in northern Iran.
1791: Agha Mohammad Khan conquers Azerbaijan.
1792: the Qajar advance on Fars.
1794: Kerman falls and the Zand are finished.
1794: the Qajar take Fars and Kerman, ending the Zand dynasty.
1795: the Qajar besiege Shusha.
1795: Agha Mohammad Khan invades Georgia.
1795: the Shusha siege ends in a settlement on 9 August.
1796: Cliopatria draws the Erivan, Karabakh and Ganja khanates as Qajar land.
1796: Agha Mohammad Khan takes Khorasan.
1797: Cliopatria's shape adds Shirvan, Sheki and Baku.
1801: Russia annexes Kartli-Kakheti.
1804: Russia takes Ganja and the Russo-Persian war begins.
1804: Ganja falls to Russia on 15 January; its governor Javad Khan is killed.
1805: Karabakh and Shaki submit to Russia.
1805: Russia accepts the submission of Shirvan on 27 December (the year is 1805 by context).
1806: Baku is surrendered to Russia.

1813: the Treaty of Gulistan. the infobox: 'Persia is forced to cede what is now Georgia, Southern Dagestan, most of Azerbaijan' and minor parts of northern Armenia; Persia kept Meghri and the northern Talysh border was left for later decision.
1813: the first Russo-Persian war ends in a Russian victory with the Treaty of Gulistan.
1826: the second Russo-Persian war begins.
1827: Tabriz surrenders to Russia.
1828: the Russians leave Tabriz and Ardabil.
1828: the Treaty of Turkmenchay.
1828: the war ends with the Treaty of Turkmenchay (2 February 1828).
1856: Persia takes Herat.
1856: Britain lands in Persia.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1857: the Treaty of Paris, signed 4 March: the Shah 'agreed to withdraw from Herat'.
1857: the British leave Bushehr.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1909: Russia occupies Tabriz.
1910: Russia occupies Urmia and Khoi.
1915: Ottoman troops take Urmia.
1915: an Ottoman column enters Tabriz about a week after Urmia fell (4 January 1915).
1915: Russia retakes Tabriz.
1915: the Ottoman presence around Urmia ends.
1915: British forces occupy Bushehr in August 1915 and later raise the South Persia Rifles (1916); the British advance reached Kerman on 12 June 1916.
1915: the Russian army spreads across northern Persia.
1916: the Ottoman XIII Corps invades Persia.
1916: the Russians retake the Hamadan front. in December 1916 Russian forces retook Qom and Hamadan; the page does not say when the Ottomans left Kermanshah.
1917: the Russian occupation of Tabriz collapses.
1917: the Russian occupation of Urmia and Khoi ends with the collapse of the Russian army ('no effective military force' for the rest of 1917).
1917: the Russian zone across northern Persia dissolves; about 1,000 loyal Cossacks under Baratov still helped the British in February 1918.
1918: British forces reach northern Persia.
1918: the Ottoman IV Corps re-enters Persia.
1918: the Armistice of Mudros (30 October 1918) ends the Ottoman occupation of northern Persia; the infobox lists the Ottoman withdrawal.
1920: Soviet ships enter Anzali.
1920: Mirza Kuchik Khan's Jangali partisans set up the Persian Socialist Soviet Republic in Gilan with Red Army help, capital Rasht.
1921: the British occupation of the south ends.
1921: the British occupation of the north ends.
1921: Soviet forces withdraw after the Russo-Persian treaty of February 1921, which 'ensured peaceful relations' and resulted in 'the withdrawal of Soviet forces'.
1921: the Gilan republic is crushed.
1925: the Majles deposes Ahmad Shah and the Qajar dynasty ends.

wars.name: Qajar-Zand wars
wars.outcome: Qajar victory: Lotf Ali Khan Zand is defeated at Kerman in 1794 (the city fell on 24 October) and the Zand dynasty ends.

wars.name: Persian invasion of Georgia (1795)
wars.outcome: Agha Mohammad Khan took and sacked Tbilisi on 11 September 1795; Russia annexed Kartli-Kakheti in 1801.

wars.name: Russo-Persian War (1804-1813)
wars.outcome: Russian victory: the Treaty of Gulistan (24 October 1813) cedes Georgia, Southern Dagestan and most of Azerbaijan; Persia keeps Meghri, Erivan and Nakhchivan.

wars.name: Russo-Persian War (1826-1828)
wars.outcome: Russian victory: the Treaty of Turkmenchay (2 February 1828) takes the last Persian lands north of the Aras and a large indemnity.

wars.name: Anglo-Persian War
wars.outcome: British victory: Persia withdraws from Herat under the Treaty of Paris (4 March 1857) and the British leave the Gulf ports.

wars.name: Persian campaign (World War I)
wars.outcome: Allied victory with British control; Persia stayed neutral and kept its frontier.

wars.name: Soviet intervention in Gilan
wars.outcome: The Soviet fleet lands at Anzali in May 1920 and the Persian Socialist Soviet Republic holds Gilan until September 1921, when Reza Khan's government ends it.

certainty.note: The frontiers with the Caucasus khanates, Georgia and the Durrani lands in Khorasan are tribal and vassal lines, not surveyed; the Aras becomes a treaty line only in 1828.
The Russian frontier is a treaty line: the Aras from Turkmenchay (1828) and the Atrek from the Treaty of Akhal (1881).
Foreign armies occupy Persian land in 1909-21 and the central government controls little of the periphery; the pre-war frontier itself is unchanged.
